record.original_question: Lusztig’s “Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture” about the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomialsP x,y(q): Let (W 1, S1),(W 2, S2) be two Coxeter systems, andu≤vinW 1,w≤zinW 2 (in the strong Bruhat order) be such that [u, v]≃[w, z] (the intervals in the Strong Bruhat order are isomorphic as posets). Then prove Pu,v(q) =P w,z(q).

evidence.quote: [Bren2024, Conj. 1.4] Lusztig’s “Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture” about the Kazhdan–Lusztig polyno- mialsP x,y(q): Let (W 1, S1),(W 2, S2) be two Coxeter systems, andu≤vinW 1,w≤zinW 2 (in the strong Bruhat order) be such that [u, v]≃[w, z] (the intervals in the Strong Bruhat order are isomorphic as posets). Then prove Pu,v(q) =P w,z(q).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(W_1, S_1)$ and $(W_2, S_2)$ be two Coxeter systems. For a Coxeter system $(W,S)$, the (strong) Bruhat order on $W$ is the partial order generated by the relation $w < ws$ whenever $\ell(ws) > \ell(w)$ for some reflection $s$ (equivalently, $u \le v$ iff some/every reduced expression for $v$ contains a subword that is a reduced expression for $u$). For $u \le v$ in $W$, the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $P_{u,v}(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q]$ is the unique polynomial of degree at most $\tfrac{1}{2}(\ell(v)-\ell(u)-1)$ characterized by the Kazhdan–Lusztig recursion in the Hecke algebra of $(W,S)$, with $P_{u,u}(q) = 1$.

Given $u \le v$ in $W_1$ and $w \le z$ in $W_2$ such that the Bruhat intervals $[u,v] = \{x \in W_1 : u \le x \le v\}$ and $[w,z] = \{y \in W_2 : w \le y \le z\}$ are isomorphic as posets, prove that
$$P_{u,v}(q) = P_{w,z}(q).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture of Lusztig and Dyer remains open in general as of 2025–2026. Substantial partial progress has been made: it is known for lower intervals, for elementary intervals in symmetric groups (Barkley–Gaetz, Math. Ann. 2025), in small-rank/finite cases, and for the parabolic analog in various cases (Esposito et al.). A hypercube-decomposition program (Blundell–Buesing–Davies–Veličković–Williamson, arXiv:2111.15161) gives a conjectural framework but does not resolve the general conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Towards combinatorial invariance for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: We outline a conjectural strategy via hypercube decompositions for proving the combinatorial invariance conjecture for symmetric groups.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open; only a conjectural framework provided.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial invariance for Kazhdan–Lusztig R-polynomials of elementary intervals
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture for R-polynomials in the case of elementary intervals in S_n, generalizing the lower interval case.
status_evidence.claim: Proved only for a special class of intervals, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: A note on combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials (Esposito, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent note giving partial results on combinatorial invariance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial result, full conjecture still open.
